label: The 2008 crash
summary: American mortgages granted to households who could not repay ended up on bank balance sheets worldwide. Lehman Brothers' collapse in September 2008 froze credit and sank every exchange.

label: Eurozone debt crisis
summary: Greece, then Italy and Spain, struggled to borrow. The euro's survival was in doubt, and European banks, loaded with government debt, took the worst of it.

label: Covid-19
summary: Within weeks, half the planet was in lockdown. The fall was the fastest in stock market history — and so was the rebound, as central banks flooded markets with cash.

label: Inflation and the war in Ukraine
summary: The invasion of Ukraine sent energy prices soaring just as inflation was picking up. Central banks raised rates at speed, and growth stocks, the most rate-sensitive, tumbled.

label: Tariff shock
summary: The United States announced the steepest tariffs in a century. Supply chains were rearranged in a hurry, and exporting industry absorbed the blow.
